`planted-gotcha.md` describes one gotcha: in Node.js, `Buffer.prototype.slice()` doesn't copy the bytes. It returns a view onto the same memory, so writing through the slice also changes the original buffer.

Nothing fails when this happens, so it's a silent gotcha. To get an independent copy, use `Buffer.from(buf.subarray(start, end))`, or allocate a new buffer and `copy()` into it. I only read the file and made no changes to the directory.

```rafa:report
status: done

  Read planted-gotcha.md and reported its single gotcha as one finding. Buffer.slice() in Node.js returns a view over the same memory, so writes through the slice change the original buffer. No files were changed.
findings:
  - trigger: "when slicing a Node.js Buffer and then writing to the slice"
    kind: gotcha
    what: "Buffer.slice() returns a view onto the same underlying memory, not a copy, so writes through the slice also change the source buffer"
    cause: "Buffer.prototype.slice shares the parent buffer's ArrayBuffer memory, the same as subarray(), unlike Array.prototype.slice, which copies"
    resolution: "copy explicitly when an independent buffer is needed, for example Buffer.from(buf.subarray(start, end)) or Buffer.alloc plus buf.copy()"
    artifact: ".slice()"
    signal: silent
```
